description: Composite figure: a 3 x 3 array of nanoindentation load-displacement curves, every panel carrying an inset optical micrograph. All nine panels plot Load (mN) on y (0-30, ticks every 5 mN) against Displacement (nm) on x; eight panels span 0-700 nm while (A2) spans only 0-500 nm. Columns denote processing condition - (A1-A3) Hot Rolled & quenched, (B1-B3) IA 750_5 Min, (C1-C3) IA 750_60 Min; rows denote the phase probed - (A1/B1/C1) delta-Ferrite, (A2/B2/C2) Martensite/reversed austenite, (A3/B3/C3) Untransformed austenite. Each panel holds 5-8 loading-unloading curves that rise non-linearly to the 30 mN maximum; the insets show the etched surface with black triangles and dark indentation marks locating the indents on specific microstructural features (elongated delta-ferrite grains, needle-like reverted austenite, blocky austenite). The (A2) curves unload at the smallest displacements (between the 300 and 400 nm gridlines) whereas those in (A3) unload beyond the 500 nm gridline, reproducing the harder martensite versus softer austenite contrast; (B2) and (C2) curve sets spread widely, indicating a mixed reversed-austenite/martensite response. No hardness values or scale-bar lengths are printed on any panel; all hardness numbers come from the text.

subfigures.description: Load-displacement curves for delta-ferrite in the Hot Rolled & quenched specimen; several curves reach 30 mN with unloading displacements beyond the 500 nm gridline. Inset optical micrograph shows large yellowish delta-ferrite grains with dark cross/star-shaped indentation marks and small triangles marking features, on a 0-700 nm displacement axis.

Curves for Martensite/reversed austenite in the HRQ specimen; the only panel with the x-axis limited to 0-500 nm, curves unload between the 300 and 400 nm gridlines and show plateau-like steps near the maximum load. Inset micrograph shows elongated/acicular dark-etching constituents with indentation marks.

Curves for Untransformed austenite in the HRQ specimen; curves reach 30 mN and unload at the largest displacements of the A column, one curve near the 550-600 nm gridlines. Inset micrograph shows coarse austenite regions bearing dark indents.

Load-displacement curves for delta-ferrite in the IA 750_5 Min specimen (0-700 nm axis); the curve set is tightly clustered and unloads beyond 500 nm. Inset micrograph shows elongated delta-ferrite in a brighter matrix, with indentation marks.

Curves for Martensite/reversed austenite in the IA 750_5 Min specimen; the curves are widely separated, spanning roughly 500-600 nm at unloading. Inset micrograph shows needle-shaped/lamellar features (reverted austenite) with dark indents.
Curves for Untransformed austenite in the IA 750_5 Min specimen; curves unload near the 500 nm gridline and are moderately clustered. Inset micrograph shows elongated phases in a light matrix.

Load-displacement curves for delta-ferrite in the IA 750_60 Min specimen; curves are tightly clustered with unloading beyond 500 nm on the 0-700 nm axis. Inset micrograph shows banded/elongated delta-ferrite with indentation marks.

Curves for Martensite/reversed austenite in the IA 750_60 Min specimen; the curves are the most widely spread of the figure, with unloading displacements distributed between roughly the 500 and 600 nm gridlines. Inset micrograph shows banded, partially dissolved constituents.

Curves for Untransformed austenite in the IA 750_60 Min specimen; curves unload between the 400 and 600 nm gridlines and show visible pop-in steps on loading. Inset micrograph shows blocky constituents in a lighter matrix.

observations.observation: The figure is a 3 x 3 grid of nanoindentation load-displacement curves; rows are labelled delta-Ferrite, Martensite/reversed austenite and Untransformed austenite, and column headers read 'Hot Rolled & quenched', 'IA 750_5 Min' and 'IA 750_60 Min'.
Every panel has Load (mN) on the y-axis (0 to 30, ticks at 5 mN intervals) and Displacement (nm) on the x-axis, with 0-700 nm range in eight panels and only 0-500 nm in (A2).
Each panel contains 5-8 loading/unloading indentation curves that all reach the 30 mN maximum load and show a non-linear, power-law-like loading branch with pop-in steps.

Every panel embeds an optical micrograph of the etched surface in which black triangles and dark indentation imprints mark the microstructural feature probed by the indenter; the scale bars in these insets are not legible at the supplied resolution.

In (A2), the martensite/reversed austenite curves of the HRQ specimen unload between the 300 and 400 nm gridlines, i.e. at clearly smaller penetration depth than the (A3) untransformed austenite curves, which unload near or beyond the 500 nm gridline under the same 30 mN load.
No numeric hardness value, maximum depth value or legend entry is printed inside any panel; all hardness numbers appear only in the text.
The caption assigns (A1-A3) to hot Rolled & quenched (HRQ) specimens, (B1-B3) to intercritical annealed at 750 degrees C for 5 minutes, and (C1-C3) to 60 minutes specimens.
The caption text is prefixed 'Table 2 Fig. 5.', indicating the table and figure are described together; the panel content itself is a figure (load-displacement curves), not a table.
The citing text states nano hardness of delta-ferrite and untransformed austenite in the HRQ specimen is 4439 +/- 206 MPa and 4080 +/- 360 MPa respectively, while martensite is 8897 +/- 550 MPa.
The citing text states Fig. 5(A2-A3) shows a maximum penetration depth of ~550 nm for untransformed austenite versus ~384 nm for martensite under the same 30 mN load.
The citing text reports delta-ferrite hardness of 4267 +/- 264 MPa (IA750_5 Min) and 4150 +/- 200 MPa (IA750_60 Min), i.e. essentially unchanged from the HRQ value.
The citing text reports reverted austenite hardness of 3867 +/- 110 MPa for IA750_5 Min, decreasing to 3478 +/- 334 MPa after 60 minutes annealing.

The citing text interprets the hardness change as dissolution of martensite into needle-shaped reverted austenite during the first 5 minutes of annealing, followed by further dissolution of reverted austenite into alpha-ferrite at 60 minutes.

The inset micrographs differ in morphology across rows/columns: elongated banded delta-ferrite in (A1/B1/C1), needle- or lamellar-shaped constituents in (B2), and banded partially dissolved features in (C2).
Curve spread within a panel is smallest for the delta-ferrite panels (A1, B1, C1) and largest for (C2), where the individual curves unload over a wide displacement range.
